title: What asbestos training does OSHA require outside construction?
description: OSHA 1910.1001(j)(7) asbestos training: PEL trigger, annual cycle, ten topics, housekeeping awareness and construction class contrast, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) general industry asbestos standard, 29 CFR 1910.1001(j)(7), requires training for every employee exposed at or above the permissible exposure limit or excursion limit, before or at initial assignment and at least annually. Employees doing housekeeping where asbestos-containing material is present need a separate annual awareness course. Construction is governed instead by 29 CFR 1926.1101, which sets training by work class, from 2 hours for Class IV to EPA accredited courses for Class I.
keyTakeaways: The general industry trigger is exposure at or above 0.1 fiber per cubic centimeter as an 8-hour TWA, or the excursion limit of 1.0 f/cc over 30 minutes.
Training is required prior to or at initial assignment and at least annually under 1910.1001(j)(7)(ii), and must be delivered in a manner the employee can understand.
Housekeeping staff in areas with asbestos-containing or presumed asbestos-containing material need an annual awareness course, at no cost, under (j)(7)(iv).
Training records must be kept for one year beyond the employee's last date of employment under 1910.1001(m)(4).
Construction asbestos training under 1926.1101(k)(9) is tied to four work classes and sets minimum course lengths of 8, 16 and 2 hours for some classes.
jurisdiction: United States (federal, with state plan variations)
regulator: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), US Department of Labor
appliesTo: General industry employers with occupational asbestos exposure, such as brake and clutch repair, manufacturing using asbestos products, and facility operations in older buildings
Employees exposed at or above the asbestos PEL or excursion limit
Housekeeping and custodial employees working in areas containing asbestos-containing material (ACM) or presumed asbestos-containing material (PACM)
Not construction work (29 CFR 1926.1101) or shipyard employment (29 CFR 1915.1001)

sections.heading: Which asbestos standard covers which employers?

blocks.text: Three OSHA asbestos standards divide the economy by type of work. [29 CFR 1910.1001](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1001) applies to all occupational asbestos exposure in industries covered by the Occupational Safety and Health Act, except construction work, which paragraph (a)(2) sends to 29 CFR 1926.1101, and ship repairing, shipbuilding and shipbreaking, which paragraph (a)(3) sends to 29 CFR 1915.1001.

The distinction matters because the same building can generate both kinds of work. A facility's custodians cleaning around intact pipe insulation are typically in general industry. A contractor removing that insulation is doing construction work and falls under the class system described below.

Paragraph (j)(7)(i) requires training for each employee "exposed to airborne concentrations of asbestos at or above the PEL and/or excursion limit." Paragraph (c) sets the permissible exposure limit (PEL) at 0.1 fiber per cubic centimeter of air as an 8-hour time-weighted average, and the excursion limit at 1.0 fiber per cubic centimeter averaged over a sampling period of 30 minutes.

Paragraph (j)(7)(ii) sets the timing: training "shall be provided prior to or at the time of initial assignment and at least annually thereafter." Paragraph (j)(7)(iii) requires the program to be conducted in a manner the employee is able to understand.

sections.heading: What must general industry asbestos training cover?

blocks.text: Paragraph (j)(7)(iii) lists ten topics, labeled (A) through (J). They are:

items: The health effects associated with asbestos exposure.
The relationship between smoking and exposure to asbestos producing lung cancer.
The quantity, location, manner of use, release and storage of asbestos, and the specific operations that could result in exposure.
The engineering controls and work practices associated with the employee's job assignment.
The specific procedures implemented to protect employees, such as work practices, emergency and clean-up procedures, and personal protective equipment.
The purpose, proper use and limitations of respirators and protective clothing, if appropriate.
The purpose and a description of the medical surveillance program.
The content of the standard, including appendices.
The names, addresses and phone numbers of public health organizations providing smoking cessation information or programs (the list in Appendix I may be distributed).
The requirements for posting signs and affixing labels, and the meaning of the required legends.

blocks.text: Paragraph (j)(7)(v) adds access duties: a copy of the standard and appendices readily available without cost to affected employees, all training materials provided to OSHA on request, and information to all employees about the availability of self-help smoking cessation material.

sections.heading: What training do housekeeping employees need?

blocks.text: Housekeeping employees in areas containing ACM or PACM need an annual asbestos awareness course whether or not their exposure reaches the PEL. Paragraph (j)(7)(iv) requires the course to be provided at no cost and to contain at a minimum: health effects of asbestos, locations of ACM and PACM in the building or facility, recognition of ACM and PACM damage and deterioration, the standard's housekeeping requirements, and proper response to fiber release episodes. Each such employee must be trained at least once a year.

This is the general industry provision most often missed, because it does not depend on monitoring results. A building with known or presumed asbestos materials creates the duty for its cleaning staff as soon as they work in those areas.

sections.heading: How does construction asbestos training under 1926.1101 differ?

blocks.text: Construction training is organized by the class of work rather than by exposure alone. [29 CFR 1926.1101](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1101) paragraph (b) defines Class I as removal of thermal system insulation (TSI) and surfacing ACM and PACM; Class II as removal of other ACM such as wallboard, floor tile, roofing and siding shingles and construction mastics; Class III as repair and maintenance where ACM is likely to be disturbed; and Class IV as maintenance and custodial activity that contacts but does not disturb ACM or PACM, plus cleanup of debris from Class I to III work.

blocks.text: Construction also requires a designated competent person under paragraph (o). For Class I and II work, paragraph (o)(4)(i) requires a supervisor course meeting the EPA Model Accreditation Plan criteria or equivalent. Construction training records follow the same retention as general industry: one year beyond the last date of employment under (n)(4).

sections.heading: What evidence should a general industry asbestos program keep?

blocks.text: Unlike many OSHA health standards, the asbestos standard prescribes a training record retention period. Paragraph (m)(4) requires the employer to maintain all employee training records for one year beyond the last date of employment of that employee.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links a building's register of asbestos-containing and presumed asbestos-containing materials to the roles that work in each area, so the housekeeping awareness duty is identified from the location, not from monitoring alone. General industry and construction requirements are held as separate frameworks that share the underlying health effects and recognition concepts.

faqs.q: Do maintenance staff in an older building need asbestos training?
faqs.a: It depends on the work. Custodial staff in areas with ACM or PACM need the annual awareness course under 1910.1001(j)(7)(iv). Maintenance that is likely to disturb ACM is Class III construction work under 1926.1101, which requires at least 16 hours of hands-on training.

faqs.q: How long must asbestos training records be kept?
faqs.a: For one year beyond the employee's last date of employment, under 1910.1001(m)(4) in general industry and 1926.1101(n)(4) in construction. That is longer than many employers assume, because the clock starts at separation rather than at the training date.

faqs.q: Does general industry asbestos training have a minimum number of hours?
faqs.a: No. Paragraph (j)(7) lists topics but sets no hours. The minimum course lengths of 8, 16 and 2 hours appear only in the construction standard, for specific Class II, Class III and Class IV work respectively.

faqs.q: Must asbestos training include smoking cessation information?
faqs.a: Yes. Topic (B) covers the relationship between smoking and asbestos in producing lung cancer, topic (I) requires contact details of public health organizations offering smoking cessation programs, and (j)(7)(v)(C) requires employees to be told self-help material is available on request.

factCheck.claim: 1910.1001(a)(2)-(3): does not apply to construction (1926.1101) or shipyard employment (1915.1001).
1910.1001(c): PEL 0.1 f/cc 8-hour TWA; excursion limit 1.0 f/cc averaged over 30 minutes.
1910.1001(j)(7)(i)-(iii): train employees at or above PEL and/or excursion limit; prior to or at initial assignment and at least annually; understandable manner; topics (A)-(J).
1910.1001(j)(7)(iv): asbestos awareness course at no cost for housekeeping in ACM/PACM areas, five minimum elements, at least once a year; (j)(7)(v) access and smoking cessation material.
1910.1001(m)(4): training records maintained one year beyond last date of employment.
